title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Historical data at $5.20 shows only 6.6% uplift vs. baseline (32/30.1), suggesting price elasticity of ~0.88. No promotion effect observed at this price. Demand response is muted, but not zero.

drivers.name: Supply risk (short delivery)
drivers.evidence: Planner note confirms supply constraint. No past data on delivery shortfalls, but post-promotion dips (x0.83) suggest demand can drop when supply is constrained. This is a low-confidence but plausible downside driver.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.1. A 3.4% price increase to $5.20 (vs. $5.03) is a known demand-destroying driver. Historical data shows no consistent lift from past promotions (noise-adjusted effect x1.0), and the post-promotion dip is well-documented (x0.83). The recent week (2026-10-05) sold 32 units at $5.20—only 6.6% above baseline, suggesting minimal price sensitivity. However, the planner note warns of a short delivery, implying supply constraint that could reduce sales. No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no change, but the supply risk justifies a downward adjustment. Evidence is thin but consistent with supply-driven demand suppression. Shrink toward 1.0.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
